voidsworn.blurb: Frontier secessionists from the dying Vesper Reach, flying unlinked iron warships to smash Eclipse's siphons. Heavy armor, long lances, and flank batteries that hit harder on a burn.

hegemony.blurb: The core-world fleet of the Meridian Directorate: clean wedge hulls, linked crews, and drone screens. Ion cannons strip shields while carriers control the flight lanes.

corsair.blurb: Hunched, plate-faced alien raiders who hunt by thermal spike and ion wake, bolting stripped enemy armor onto dark hulls. Fast, light on shields, and loaded with rockets.

chorus.blurb: A living bio-weapon that consumed its Fleshwright makers. Zero shields, raw hull regrowth every round, acid weapons, and relentless spore swarms.

ithar.blurb: Long-lived optical engineers flying hulls of pearl and glass that split starlight into razor beams. Blindingly fast with strong shields, yet fragile the moment those shields fail.

deathless.blurb: Uploaded Starwright minds in violet-black sunshade frames, siphoning neighbor stars to build a new sun. Armor-piercing null weapons, fold drives, and wrecks that rebuild themselves.

EVENTS.b: Long-range sensors pick up an unpowered warship tumbling slowly off the lane, its outer hull scored with Starwright script nobody has translated in a millennium.

o.l: Send breach teams aboard
o.s: Risky. Could hold founders' hardware, or something still powered.

o.l: Strip outer plating from range
o.s: +35 credits, zero risk.

o.l: Core the vault cleanly with lances
o.s: Clean extraction: a refit and 40 credits, nothing wakes.

o.l: Leave it drifting
o.s: Nothing happens.

ithar.b: Long-range sensors pick up an unpowered warship tumbling off the lane. Your cataloger reads the old Starwright script on its outer hull and identifies a sealed founders' vault.

deathless.b: Long-range sensors pick up an unpowered warship tumbling off the lane. The Archive identifies the Starwright hull markings as pre-collapse and returns the vault's last recorded status: sealed.

EVENTS.b: A Directorate supply tender limps along the outer jump lane with a shattered drive ring, broadcasting an automated distress ping on every band.

o.l: Patch their drive
o.s: Grateful crew transfers 50 credits and shares local flight logs (+10 XP).

o.l: Tow them clear with a carrier
o.s: +70 credits and a Nemesis weakness revealed from their sensor logs.

o.l: Crack their cargo hold
o.s: +100 credits. Expect an elite Directorate ambush; Nemesis clock moves on 1.

o.l: Pass wide
o.s: Nothing happens.

EVENTS.b: Your signals officer isolates a clean founders' transponder pulsing from inside a jump rift. Real hardware sits on the far side, though crossing the shear will punish your hulls.

hegemony.b: Your telemetry officer decoded an old Directorate supply beacon broadcasting from inside an unstable jump rift.

corsair.b: Your best wake-tracker swears she's reading a rich alloy cache humming on the far side of a jump rift. She's right more often than not.

chorus.b: Our sensory pits catch a bright thermal spike pulsing steadily on the far side of a spatial rift.

ithar.b: Your primary mirrors catch an unmistakable Starwright optical flash coming from beyond a jump rift.

deathless.b: An encrypted Archive transponder from before Ardent's fall pulses steadily beyond a rift.

o.l: Push through the shear
o.s: Gain salvage. One random ship takes 30% hull damage.

o.l: Burn a spare refit as ablative shielding
o.s: Gain salvage. Uses one refit from the hold instead of hull damage.

o.l: Bypass the rift
o.s: Nothing happens.

o.l: Hire her (80 credits)

o.l: Offer her a slot in the Crusade line, no pay

o.l: Wave her off
o.s: Nothing happens.

o.l: Offer her a slot in the Crusade line, no pay
o.s: She takes the oath. A faction destroyer joins with veteran experience.

o.l: Leave it drifting
o.s: Nothing happens.

o.s: A veteran Eclipse destroyer rejoins the line.

o.l: Offer her a slot in the Crusade line, no pay
o.s: She takes the oath. A faction destroyer joins with veteran experience.

o.l: Leave it dormant
o.s: Nothing happens.

o.l: Offer her a slot in the Crusade line, no pay
o.s: She takes the oath. A faction destroyer joins with veteran experience.

o.l: Tell them to find another den
o.s: Nothing happens.

ithar.b: A lone Glasswright lancet emerges from dust cover, its primary mirror pitted from an old ambush. Its captain offers to join your formation if you fund the kiln-glass needed to seal her hull.

o.l: Supply the crystal stock (80 credits)
o.s: A veteran Glasswright lancet joins your fleet.

o.l: Offer her a slot in the Crusade line, no pay
o.s: She takes the oath. A faction destroyer joins with veteran experience.

o.l: Wish her clear lanes
o.s: Nothing happens.

EVENTS.b: A wall of crackling spatial shear sweeps straight across your jump lane, tearing blue-red arcs off passing dust.

o.l: Burn straight through
o.s: Every ship takes 10% hull damage.

o.l: Angle full shields forward and push
o.s: No damage. +10 XP per ship.

o.l: Plot a wide detour (40 credits)
o.s: Spend extra reaction mass to go around cleanly.

EVENTS.b: A lone crystal cruiser glides parallel to your course and pulses a quiet trade offer: one of your fitted ship refits for a rare piece of Starwright hardware.

o.l: Trade an installed refit for salvage
o.s: Lose one random installed refit. Gain salvage.

o.l: Answer in formal optical code
o.s: The keeper pulses warm amber and gifts the salvage outright. No refit lost.

o.l: Decline and keep course
o.s: Nothing happens.

EVENTS.b: An eccentric master fabricator running a hollowed-out asteroid foundry hails your bridge. He'll overhaul your roughest hull for free if your tactical officer lets him copy your combat logs.

o.l: Dock and share your logs
o.s: Your most damaged ship is fully repaired and upgraded one Mark.

o.l: Add a spare refit to the deal
o.s: Your most damaged ship is repaired and upgraded, plus a second ship is fully repaired.

o.l: Keep moving
o.s: Nothing happens.

chorus.b: A fractured volcanic rock vents dense mineral vapor along the jump lane, rich enough to calcify our heaviest hull into a tougher strain.

o.l: Bathe the most damaged hull in the plume
o.s: Your most damaged hull heals fully and evolves one Mark.

o.l: Dissolve a spare refit into the vent
o.s: Your most damaged hull heals and evolves, plus a second hull heals fully.

o.l: Move on
o.s: Nothing happens.

EVENTS.b: Chorus spores have blanketed an automated ore moon. Miners are blinking laser distress signals from the deep bore shafts while a brood-cluster swells in low orbit.

o.l: Clear orbit and break the brood
o.s: Fight an elite Chorus battle. Win salvage.

o.l: Sweep the orbital spore cloud with point defense
o.s: Pull the miners out before the brood hatches. +60 credits and +15 XP per ship.

o.l: Sterilize the shafts from orbit and leave
o.s: +20 XP per ship.

EVENTS.b: A cold memorial beacon orbits a dead mining rock, its outer plating covered in chalked crew names from an earlier Vesper expedition. Your crews ask to pause and leave supplies for the next fleet.

hegemony.b: An old frontier memorial station orbits a dead rock. Even linked spacers get superstitious this far out, and your crews request a brief tribute stop.

corsair.b: An old memorial station hangs in dead orbit, bolted over with scorched trophy plates from rival packs. Your captains want to weld a mark of their own on the hull.

ithar.b: A pre-collapse optical beacon still turns slowly over a dead moon. Your captains request time to align mirrors in tribute.

o.l: Leave 50 credits in repair stock
o.s: Morale jumps; crews patch 30% hull across every ship.

o.l: Chalk your fleet's names and move on
o.s: Even odds: +30% hull patched across the fleet, or nothing.

o.l: Leave a piece of salvage in tribute
o.s: Every ship is fully repaired and every captain gains 20 XP.

o.l: Hold schedule and jump
o.s: Nothing happens.

EVENTS.b: A battered Directorate escape pod drops out of stealth with its transponder wiped. Three junior officers aboard claim they cut their own Registry links and will share fleet firing tables for asylum.

o.l: Bring them aboard
o.s: Your least experienced captain gains 60 XP from their tactical drills.

o.l: Debrief them on the enemy commander
o.s: Least experienced captain gains 30 XP and a Nemesis weakness is revealed.

o.l: Transmit their coordinates for the bounty
o.s: +60 credits.

chorus.b: A Directorate escape pod drifts off-lane with its drive dead, still broadcasting compressed tactical logs on emergency loop.

o.l: Consume the pod and read the combat traces
o.s: Your least experienced hull gains 60 XP.

o.l: Have a senior brood-mind dissect the command codes
o.s: Least experienced hull gains 30 XP and reveals a Nemesis weakness.

o.l: Strip its high-grade alloy shell
o.s: +60 credits.

deathless.b: A Directorate escape pod pings your lead ships with an asylum request, offering stolen fleet formation data in trade.

o.l: Scan their combat logs and release the pod
o.s: Your least experienced ship gains 60 XP.

o.l: Cross-reference their logs against the Archive
o.s: Least experienced ship gains 30 XP and reveals a Nemesis weakness.

o.l: Broadcast their beacon to Meridian for salvage credit
o.s: +60 credits.

EVENTS.b: Sensors pick up a Hullbreaker hardware pod tethered inside a gas giant's dust ring, locked with clumsy mechanical seals.

o.l: Pry the hardware bay
o.s: Gain a random refit.

o.l: Crack the seals with a torpedo and drain the fuel tanks
o.s: Gain a random refit plus 45 credits.

o.l: Siphon the fuel and credits
o.s: +45 credits.

EVENTS.b: An abandoned sector customs station tumbles on reserve batteries, its hard-currency vault still sealed. The tamper relays are ancient, yet their status lamps still blink green.

o.l: Blow the vault hatches
o.s: +70 credits. The distress ping carries: Nemesis clock advances 1.

o.l: Burn through the lock cleanly with a lance
o.s: +70 credits, no alarm tripped.

o.l: Leave it sealed
o.s: Nothing happens.

EVENTS.b: Your picket pulls a drifting ejection pod out of a debris lane. Inside, a battered squadron pilot clutches a cracked flight recorder from a carrier that went down two sectors back.

o.l: Take her onto the bridge crew

o.l: Assign her to your carrier's flight ops
o.s: Your best carrier's squadrons gain a veteran perk.

o.l: Tag her pod for automated pickup

o.l: Graft it into your largest brood-sac
o.s: Your best carrier's swarms gain a veteran perk.

o.l: Let it freeze
o.s: Nothing happens.

o.s: Your least experienced ship gains 40 XP.

o.l: Upload the maneuvers into your largest carrier

o.l: Leave it pinging
o.s: Nothing happens.

o.l: Put her on a junior gunnery bridge
o.s: Your least experienced captain gains 40 XP.

o.l: Give her a bay on your best hulk-carrier

o.l: Toss the pod toward a neutral beacon
o.s: Nothing happens.

ithar.b: Sensors pick up a fading amber pulse from a crippled starling canopy drifting near an asteroid. Its pilot has kept the wing's optical telemetry alive on reserve power.

o.l: Bring the pilot onto a young cruiser
o.s: Your least experienced captain gains 40 XP.

o.l: Assign the pilot to your senior aperture
o.s: Your best carrier's wings gain a veteran perk.

o.l: Mark the beacon for passing kin
o.s: Nothing happens.

o.l: Graft a spare refit over the rupture
o.s: Uses one refit from the hold. Zero hull damage.

o.l: Let Eclipse repair drones knit the seam
o.s: Zero cost.

o.l: Shed 45 credits of dense minerals to calcify the seam
o.s: Zero hull damage.

deathless.b: Telemetry flags a micro-fracture in the containment band around your largest hull's trapped starlight core.

o.l: Bleed excess output and re-weld

o.l: Bridge the casing with a spare refit
o.s: Uses one refit from the hold. Zero damage.

o.l: Route repair drones straight to the seam

o.s: Zero damage.

EVENTS.b: A fast-moving front of charged solar particles sweeps across your route, scrambling unshielded optics and scouring bare armor.

o.l: Ride it out on bare plating
o.s: Every ship takes 8% hull damage.

o.l: Raise shields and burn straight through
o.s: Zero damage. +10 XP per ship.

o.l: Burn wide around the front (35 credits)
o.s: Zero hull damage.

o.l: Remind her which pack kept her courier intact last year

o.l: Remind her which pack kept her courier intact last year
o.s: She pays off the favor: a Nemesis weakness revealed for free.

o.l: Leave the cold metal
o.s: Nothing happens.

EVENTS.b: A cargo hauler's emergency band is screaming for help, except the static crackle repeats down to the exact millisecond every twelve seconds.

o.l: Burn in hot and grab the cargo anyway
o.s: +80 credits, though your next fight starts as an ambush.

o.l: Clear the approach mines with point defense first
o.s: Disarm the trap and clear the hold: +80 credits.

o.l: Leave the bait sitting
o.s: Nothing happens.

EVENTS.b: Thousands of translucent Chorus egg-sacs hang in the lagrange pocket between two moons, pulsing in slow thermal waves.

o.l: Sterilize the pocket with weapons fire
o.s: +20 XP per ship.

o.l: Sample the self-sealing membranes

patient.remember: We waited out the dark remembering how your {beat} cut us.

adapt.shields: Dense ablative membranes now layer our hides, dispersing focused lance heat.
adapt.pd: Thick spore curtains hang around our broods to detonate incoming torpedoes early.
adapt.armor: Calcified bone-plate now sheaths our forward ribs against ramming bows.
adapt.evasion: Lateral thruster fins have grown larger so we turn clean through your flank fire.
adapt.aim: Thermal sensory pits have widened across our bows, tracking every evasive burn.
adapt.special: Deep regrowth surges through every hull: +3 extra hull regenerated each round.

lessons.flank: Chorus hulls turn aggressively to feed and expose thinner aft chitin. Hammer their rear arcs.
lessons.ion: Chorus bio-hulls carry no shields at all, so ion bonus damage is wasted. Bring high-damage armor-piercing or incendiary fire instead.
lessons.torp: Light spore screens leave clear lanes for torpedo salvos when their hulls bunch together.
lessons.board: Their interior defense broods are thin on this strain. Counter-breach isolated hulls if you have strong boarding crews.
lessons.brawl: This cluster prefers spitting from medium range and aims poorly nose-to-nose. Close in and overwhelm them.
lessons.anchor: Their escorts fracture if the primary brood-ship drops below 60% hull. Focus the flagship.
lessons.slow: Sluggish propulsion sacs keep them from chasing fast ships. Kite their acid range and pick off stragglers.
lessons.strike: Every ship you lose anywhere in the run makes this Chorus fleet 4% tougher (up to 32%). Fight clean and protect your escorts.

meet: The glare off this dust field already shows the thin seam along your flank. Let's begin.
One careless turn opens an entire formation, and our mirrors are already angled for it.
win: Exactly where the refraction model predicted your shield would fold. Clean work.
A precise cut along an unguarded flank ends a battle before it turns ugly.
flee: Outer mirror compromised. Withdraw along the glare line and reset our approach.
This angle no longer favors us. We'll resume the duel on cleaner terms.
fall: Clean shot through the primary prism. You read the angle better than I expected.
The lens fractures. Remember what it cost to break a craft three centuries old.
cunning.again: You caught our blind arc with {beat} before; our mirrors are turned to cover it now.
cunning.remember: Every captain in my formation still studies how you broke us with {beat}.

meet: You are challenging a First Mirror of the Glasswrights. Hold steady and let's test your craft.
This engagement was framed long before your fleet exited jump. Show us what you have.
win: Our alignment held without a tremor while your line fell apart.
Clean beams, clean arcs, zero wasted shots. That's how fleet combat should look.
flee: A hairline fracture on the primary hull; we withdraw to anneal it and return sharper.
Not risking an ancestral hull on a sloppy exchange. We'll finish this later.
fall: Impossible... the primary mirror's gone... let the surviving cutters jump clear.
A rare failure of focus. The Lattice yards will remember this engagement.
proud.again: You relied on {beat} to force our retreat last time. Our shields are re-tuned to answer it.
proud.remember: I haven't forgotten the damage your {beat} inflicted on my flagship.

meet: Keep your distance if you prefer; our primary lances hold focus much farther than your batteries.
Cross open space whenever you're ready. Our alignment has already settled.
win: Waiting for you to overextend worked exactly as planned.
You rushed into our focal band and paid with your shields.
flee: Shield capacitors dropping below safe margins. Disengage and re-align elsewhere.
A careful commander knows when to preserve fragile hulls for the next hour.
fall: We held position one round too long. Let the remaining ships clear the debris.
Focus broken. Three centuries of patience ended in a single volley.
patient.again: Your earlier push with {beat} forced us to adjust our stand-off range. Come try it again.
patient.remember: We've spent every jump since calibrating against your {beat}.

meet: Your damaged hulls glow brightest on our optical plot, so we'll dismantle those first.
Once a hull's shields fail, the rest comes apart effortlessly. Watch closely.
win: Your weakened escorts went dark first, and your command ship couldn't cover them.
Surgical dismantling from the softest hull upward. Clean and quiet.
flee: Not clean enough; we break off before your return fire cracks an irreplaceable frame.
Withdraw and hone the arrays. Your damaged hulls won't stay patched forever.
fall: Miscalculated your armor depth... our primary prism's shattering!
You held together under focused fire better than any metal fleet had a right to.
cruel.again: Still counting on {beat} to protect your wounded hulls? We've adjusted our beams to bypass it.
cruel.remember: We still have the optical replay of how you used {beat} against us.

adapt.shields: Re-tuned prism matrices now split incoming lance frequencies across the shield pool.
adapt.pd: Mirror veils deployed along every hull to scatter torpedo guidance locks.
adapt.armor: Reinforced waveguide spines fitted to survive close-in impact blows.
adapt.evasion: Recalibrated crystal vanes shift our hulls clean out of your flank battery arcs.
adapt.aim: Interferometer lenses locked onto your drive signature; evasive burns won't hide you now.
adapt.special: Deeper optical veil active: every Glasswright hull is 6 harder to hit.

lessons.flank: Glasswright duelists rely on speed and expose their rear arcs during sharp turns. Punish them mid-pivot.
lessons.ion: Their massive shields are their entire lifeline, and brittle emitters collapse fast under ion fire.
lessons.torp: Light point defense lets fast torpedo salvos land if you force them to turn across your nose.
lessons.board: Fragile crystal hulls carry small crews. Breach isolated escorts once their shields drop.
lessons.brawl: Built for stand-off lances, they lose accuracy in a tight brawl. Close inside two hexes.
lessons.anchor: Drop the flagship's shields and push it under 60% hull to force an early withdrawal.
lessons.slow: Damaged drives rob them of their vane evasion bonus. Pin their movement and focus fire.
lessons.strike: This duelist runs a small elite fleet and retreats once its flagship loses shields and drops under 60% hull, returning sharper each time.

meet: Rushing won't save your hulls. Every century we wait, your kind forgets another mistake we still remember.
Take as many turns as you need to close. After a thousand years in the dark, a few extra minutes mean nothing.
win: Your fleet failed right where our earlier engagement models predicted.
Steady arcs, unbroken hulls. Patience always outlasts haste.
fall: This chassis fails, yet the backup stream is already spinning up a fresh frame.
Break the metal all you like; I will wake again before your welders cool.
fall_final: Even at Ardent's rim, one restoration remains. Prepare for a second fight.
The Archive authorizes one final chassis before cutoff. Let us finish this properly.
patient.again: My restored mind reviewed every volley of your {beat} before this chassis even left the rack.
patient.remember: Restoration strips minor noise away, yet it never erases a defeat to {beat}.

meet: My flagship leads the approach, just as it did when Ardent still burned overhead.
I never hide behind escorts; that held on my first chassis, and it holds on this one.
win: Our forward plates held without yielding a hex, as they have for ten centuries.
You tested an Archive flagship head-on and learned why our frames endured.
fall: My bow breaks, yet the mind inside walks straight into the next frame.
A costly breach, nothing more. The Archive will have me back on your lane shortly.
fall_final: Even here at the rim, I rise once more, flagship first, to settle this.
One last chassis left in the rack. Come finish what you started!
proud.again: The frame that returns today was armored specifically after watching your {beat} crack the last one.
proud.remember: Pride survives restoration intact, and so does the sting of your {beat}.

meet: We'll burn your crippled ships down first so the healthy crews watch what's coming.
Wounded hulls lose armor fast; our corona arcs will clear them off the plot before we touch your flagship.
win: Your damaged hulls collapsed first, and the rest couldn't hold without them.
Clean dismantling. We'll archive your surviving bridge logs as a keepsake.
fall: An interruption only. My next chassis will pick up right where this volley ended.
Enjoy the breathing room while my replacement frame spins up.
fall_final: I rise one final time to put your fleet in cold storage instead.
One last chassis, one final pass at Ardent's rim. Make your shots count.
cruel.again: You saved your crippled ships with {beat} last time. My arcs are tuned to cut through it now.
cruel.remember: Every scar from your {beat} sits fresh in my restored combat memory.

meet: Every maneuver your fleet can execute has been tested against older enemies than you.
Our advance is measured and our firing lanes are set. Proceed.
win: Your hulls folded cleanly inside our firing geometry.
Advance, fire, verify cutoff. Another obstruction cleared from the siphon lane.
fall: Frame integrity lost. The next hull advances along the exact same vector.
This chassis stops here; the replacement is already downloading our telemetry.
fall_final: One reserve chassis remains active. Executing final engagement sequence.
Final restoration online. After this fight, one of us stays dark permanently.
methodical.again: My restored telemetry patched the exact gap your {beat} exploited last time.
methodical.remember: Hulls wear out, yet the Archive retains every detail of your {beat}.

adapt.shields: Corona-ward layers installed over our hull bands to absorb your focused beams.
adapt.pd: Null spires calibrated from archived intercepts; your torpedoes will detonate short.
adapt.armor: Heavier sunshade plating bolted forward. Ramming this bow will only wreck yours.
adapt.evasion: Fold-drive micro-skips retimed so your flank volleys strike empty vacuum.
adapt.aim: Long-memory optics aligned to your thruster curve; evasive turns won't break lock.
adapt.special: Deep backup relays online: one additional fallen Eclipse ship can reassemble.

lessons.flank: Heavy Eclipse cruisers turn slowly and leave their rear bands thin. Fold or burn behind them on the turn.
lessons.ion: Eclipse frames carry no shields at all, so ion bonus damage is wasted. Bring high-pierce hull weapons and focus down wrecks.
lessons.torp: Limited null-spire coverage gives torpedoes clean approaches if you overwhelm one flank.
lessons.board: Their boarding defense is thin on freshly restored frames. Breach them right after they reassemble.
lessons.brawl: Built around slow corona volleys at mid-range, they struggle when surrounded inside two hexes.
lessons.anchor: Focus the flagship down below 60% hull to fracture escort morale.
lessons.slow: Heavy armor slows their cruise burn. Control the lanes and focus one hull at a time so swarms can't rebuild all of them.
lessons.strike: This commander's clock advances slowly, never retreats, rises once in sector 3, and drains 6% hull across your fleet when the hunt triggers.

meet: Forty worlds are freezing behind us, and you're standing in our jump lane! Open fire!
We swore back in Vesper orbit we'd burn straight through anyone blocking the sun! Come on!
win: Lane's clear! Chalk the victory on the bulkhead and check our fuel!
Tried to stop a Crusade line and paid for it! Keep moving sunward!
fall: Flagship's going up... don't stop for us, keep pushing toward the siphon!
Bulkheads are gone! Chalk my name under the others and finish the job!
zealous.again: You beat us with {beat} last time, alright, so we're hitting twice as hard today!
zealous.remember: My gunners still have your {beat} chalked beside the loading rails. Nobody forgot.

meet: This flagship has led the dawn watch through three sectors! Answer our challenge or break!
I fly right up front where every captain can see my radiators. Come test our iron!
win: Our front line held every shot you had and broke your fleet clean in half!
Looked straight down our flank guns and blinked first! Keep pushing!
fall: Front hull's buckling... close the gap over us and don't let them pass!
Damn fine shooting... the Crusade doesn't stop for one broken flagship!
proud.again: Thought {beat} would fold my front line twice? We braced every bulkhead for it!
proud.remember: I still carry the dents your {beat} put on my bow, and I mean to return them.

meet: Look at those leaking escorts on your flank. We're burning the weak ones down first!
Tag their most damaged hull and pour every flank gun into it until it cracks!
win: Took your crippled hulls off the plot first and watched the rest fold!
Every scorched hull goes on the roll. Keep the burners hot!
fall: Reactor's failing... guess your wounded ones had more fight left than I figured...
Bad way to go out... tell Vesper the cold won't be kinder to them either...
cruel.again: You kept your damaged hulls alive with {beat} before. We're cutting straight through that trick now!
cruel.remember: Still remember how you used {beat} to save those crippled escorts.

meet: Screens at full, guns laid by hand, intervals locked. Advance on my mark.
Every firing lane is measured and every crew knows their station. Engage.
win: Clean volleys, steady screens, minimal hull losses. That's how you cross three sectors.
Formation held from start to finish. Patch the burns and plot the next jump.
fall: Command hull's failing. Transfer the flag to the senior cruiser and keep the line closed.
One gap in the line, not the whole Crusade. Hold steady and finish the fight.
methodical.again: We drilled against your {beat} tactics every watch since our last fight.
methodical.remember: My tactical plot still carries the firing angles from your {beat}.

adapt.shields: Reinforced screen drills active. Your focused beams won't crack us easily now.
adapt.pd: Spark flak crews doubled across the line. Expect your torpedoes to detonate early.
adapt.armor: Riveted extra black-iron plate onto our bows. Try ramming that.
adapt.evasion: Running lighter thruster trims across the line so your flank volleys miss wide.
adapt.aim: Hand-laid optical sights zeroed in on your burn profile. Quit dodging, we've got you.
adapt.special: Crews running hot on battle rations and grit: +8% damage across all guns.

lessons.flank: Crusade cruisers commit hard to forward charges and leave thin rear armor exposed. Swing behind them.
lessons.ion: Their front screens are strong, yet brittle emitters collapse fast under sustained ion fire.
lessons.torp: Sparse point defense leaves clear torpedo lanes once their escorts commit to the flank.
lessons.board: Green breach defense crews struggle if you isolate a cruiser away from its escorts.
lessons.brawl: Their hand-laid guns lose tracking speed inside two hexes. Close in and force a knife-fight.
lessons.anchor: Their escorts fight around the flagship's example. Drive it below 60% hull to break their nerve.
lessons.slow: Heavy iron hulls burn sluggishly on worn drives. Cut off their pivots and pound their sterns.
lessons.strike: This commander holds until the flagship falls and withdraws before sector III. They challenge your flagship to single combat (+20% damage both ways). Screen your flagship or turn the duel back on them.

o.t: Overcharge the flagship with Seren's core fire
o.tx: Your engineers bleed Seren's thermal charge straight into the flagship's main bus. Every gun on the hull runs white-hot for the coming battle, though the heat buckles a quarter of the inner bulkheads before you even cross the jump.

o.t: Keep the reactors clean and patch the fleet
o.tx: You lock the core casing shut and put the welders on standard hull repairs instead. The Roll-master nods once; the gunnery crews grumble over their cooling coils, though every ship enters the rim intact.

lines: Roll-master: "There's the siphon relay, Admiral, drinking Vesper's light straight across the black hole's rim. The last expedition overdrove their flagship with Seren's charge right here."
Captain: "And did they make it home?"
Roll-master: "No. They cracked the outer collector rings wide enough for us to reach it, though. Your call whether we pay the same price or fight it cold."
voidsworn.debrief: Every captain chalked the fleet's decision beside their helm station before entering firing range.
voidsworn.learning: Win or lose, the next expedition out of Vesper will pull your flight recorders from the rim and build their approach around what worked here.

spotlights.vex: Vex checks the chalked crew roll beside the dorsal airlock before every jump, quietly adding a single date beneath the last column.
spotlights.malek: Torben runs a gloved hand along the loaded torpedo rails. 'Every warhead in this bay is paid for by a frozen farm moon back in the Reach.'
spotlights.ashgrove: Ashgrove taps her headset mic as the launch lights turn amber. 'Tight lanes, kids. Bring those fighters back to my rails in one piece.'
spotlights.thale: Thale pours lukewarm tea from a battered thermos while the proximity alarms chirp. 'Meridian wrote Vesper off seventy years ago. Let's make them check their math again.'

o.t: Cut the Registry links for one minute and speak to the crews
o.tx: Every officer drops off the Meridian net simultaneously. Without live telemetry, your synchronized fire lags on round one, yet the crews hear their admiral speak without a Registry timestamp for the first time in the campaign.

o.t: Stay linked and secure the rim by the book
o.tx: Every link stays green, Meridian credits your operational ledger for strict compliance, and the column locks into formation at the Hollow Sun perimeter. Your flag captain folds the paper casualty list back into her jacket without comment.

lines: Flag captain: "Admiral, we are within visual range of the Hollow Sun perimeter. Before a decisive engagement, line commanders customarily drop their Registry links for sixty seconds."
Flag captain: "The names of the crews we lost reaching this sector, Admiral. Meridian only archives serial numbers."
hegemony.debrief: Meridian updated its casualty projection for the Hollow Sun perimeter twice during the fight, without attaching an explanation.
hegemony.learning: Regardless of the outcome, an unsigned addendum enters the Directorate tactical manual via slow courier, arriving one sector late and still saving more crews than the official projection.

spotlights.kassar: Kassar runs two extra timing drills before the approach. 'Clean volleys end battles quickly, and short battles cost fewer hulls.'
spotlights.vorn: Vorn wipes three conservative firing plots off the holotable until only one razor-thin intercept remains. 'That is the shot that breaks their command deck.'
spotlights.reyes: Reyes broadcasts Meridian's predicted squadron loss rate over the flight channel so every pilot knows the exact number they intend to beat.
spotlights.maren: Maren inspects every bow deflector reading himself before strapping in. 'Meridian tracks tonnage. I track who gets off my ship at Meridian Yards.'

o.t: Hold heavy guns off the core and breach for Rook intact
o.tx: Your gunners hold fire on the core's containment cage while your flagship eats the return salvo head-on. If your crews drag Rook out of those wrecks in chains, every den in the Ashfall will hear about it.

o.t: Open every weapon and smash straight through
o.tx: Nobody holds back for clean salvage. Your crews push the reactors red-hot and tear into the enemy line full tilt, ready to crack the wrecks and Rook right along with them if that's what winning takes.

lines: Howler: "Scope lock confirmed, Warlord! R-5 Rook's sitting right in the middle of that wreck pile, pulsing hotter than a cruiser core!"
Warlord: "Good! Means we didn't haul all this iron across three sectors for nothing. Arm the breach clamps!"
corsair.debrief: No cheering on the open band after the guns cool. Just captains tallying kills, hauling intact plates, and checking who didn't make it back.
corsair.learning: The plates bolted to your hulls tell the whole belt what worked out here, and the next pack that hunts the Hollow Sun will study every weld seam.

spotlights.grax: Grax slams the throttle past the redline and laughs over open comms as the breach clamps bite into enemy plate, half the pack howling back on the same channel.
spotlights.sable: Sable kills all exterior lights until only the red cockpit glow remains. 'Big proud ships always forget to armor their radiator vents.'
spotlights.mott: Old Mott spits a chewed rivet pin into a scrap bucket and checks the bay telemetry. 'Forty captains tried taking my command chair. Don't make me count to forty-two today.'
spotlights.vesh: Vesh zooms the tactical feed onto the opposing flagship's bow trim, muttering measurements to her weld crew. 'Don't you dare slag that dorsal array!'

o.t: Let Memory call out to the Lattice cores
o.tx: Memory reaches toward the Hollow Sun using the dead Fleshwrights' old access codes, and a dormant core responds with fresh protocols. Yet the borrowed maker cadence makes our hunter broods hesitate a fraction of a second on the kill.

o.t: Drown Memory and let Hunger take full control
o.tx: We clamp the old maker voices shut under layers of fresh tissue. The swarm surges forward faster and cleaner, pure thermal predation aimed straight at the cores.

lines: Memory: "Ardent's ruins... our makers grew us in cold vats to punish Eclipse for killing this star. We still remember their control ciphers."
Hunger: "Ciphers don't fill brood-sacs. Five hot cores sit right behind that fleet. Tear through!"
The Swarm: "One choice shapes the next clutch we hatch."
chorus.debrief: Every brood-chamber in the swarm absorbs the chemical shift before the spores even settle.
chorus.learning: Win or lose, the next swarm grown from our surviving spores carries that balance straight into its neural sacs.

spotlights.matriarch: The Matriarch opens all nine brood-valves toward the black hole's rim, drinking the stray radiation while her young stir against the membranes.
spotlights.razormaw: Red Undertow surges ahead of the main cluster with scorched hull plating still stuck to its forward spines, impatient to close.
spotlights.mending: The Mending Throng knits fresh chitin across every scarred seam between jumps, keeping the swarm whole for the final push.
spotlights.voice: Under the wet thrum of acid sacs, the Voice broadcasts a single broken Starwright launch coordinate that makes enemy sensors glitch.

ithar.t: The Last Lens & the Killing Flaw

o.t: Fly the corrected slow arc to avoid the old trap
o.tx: You swing the fleet along the corrected vector your ancestors paid for with their ships. {rival} spots the wider approach early, yet you enter the lens's orbit knowing the exact firing blind spot that killed the first voyage.

o.t: Hold the fast burn straight for the lens mounting
o.tx: You commit at full speed straight down the hazardous lane to deny {rival} time to fortify the lens. Every captain runs razor-thin tolerances, shaving past the exact debris field that claimed the old fleet.

lines: Lens-keeper: "There hangs the last primary lens of Ardent, Captain, and our recorders just pulled the full optical replay of the fleet that died trying to recover it three centuries ago."
Captain: "They turned too early into the mounting's shadow."
Lens-keeper: "Exactly. Take the wide correction and lose surprise, or gamble our shields on outrunning the same mistake."
ithar.debrief: Every bridge crew watched the old optical replay before locking weapons, their inlays pulsing pale violet in quiet tribute.
ithar.learning: Whether this fleet carries the lens home or breaks apart in the debris belt, the optical forge will pull your telemetry and cast the next expedition sharper.

spotlights.aelith: Tamsa fans her starling wings wide around the aperture bays, checking every flight vector through rippling bands of blue-white light.
spotlights.vaelen: Saro says nothing across three full minutes of approach, adjusting the primary mirror by fractions of a degree until the focal line locks dead center.
spotlights.thorne: Vell tilts the outer vanes into the black hole's halo, splitting the flagship's silhouette into four clean radar ghosts.
spotlights.mirelle: Brin brings the prism wards up to full brilliance around the smaller escorts, refusing to let another family line end on this rim.

o.t: Reserve the last clean Archive sync for the command frame
o.tx: You lock the high-bandwidth uplink onto the flagship's bridge core before committing to the stellar frame. If the command hull breaks, your tactical memory survives intact; the escort minds go in knowing they'll wake missing months.

o.t: Spread the Archive pass across the escort crews
o.tx: You divert the backup window and repair swarms across every escort in the line, leaving your own mind running on an older stamp. 'If I wake up missing this sector,' you signal across the formation, 'tell me whether the new sun lit.'

lines: Flag officer: "The stellar frame sits dead ahead, Commander, waiting on the last cores. Interference from Ardent's gravity well gives us bandwidth for one clean Archive sync before contact."
Commander: "A thousand years in cold metal teaches you what's worth preserving. Allocate the window and bring the corona arcs online."
deathless.debrief: Before opening fire, every ship displayed the last optical capture of Ardent's noon across its bridge glass, holding it three seconds past regulation.
deathless.learning: Win or lose, the Archive retains this entire engagement. Eclipse won't send strangers back to Ardent's rim; it will wake this exact fleet again with every mistake corrected.

spotlights.nekhet: Aurex's monumental ring of floating plates shifts half a degree toward the stellar frame, white-gold light steady behind the visor.
spotlights.sekhmar: Vessane counts the opposing hulls one by one, verifying every hull's drone-weld tolerance against a thousand-year ignition chart.
spotlights.anuket: Ostrel trims every stray emitter down to background noise. 'Continuity takes discipline; panic is what corrupts a backup.'
spotlights.khepra: Seveth checks the twice-welded bow plates and signals ready. After two restorations, another siege at Ardent's rim feels almost routine.

reinf_ally.warn: Fleet command: a friendly ship will join you at the start of round {r}, on your side of the field.
reinf_ally.go: A friendly ship jumps in to help. It returns to its own patrol after the battle.

flare.warn: The star is flaring. At the start of round {r} every ship on both sides loses its shields for that round.
flare.go: Solar flare! Every shield on the field is down this round.

rout.d: Break their fleet. It flees once it has lost about two thirds of its strength.

ambush.d: Two enemy groups close in from both sides. Break their fleet.

defend.d: Keep enemy ships off the friendly station until round 6 ends. Every enemy ship next to the station at the start of a round knocks out 1 integrity. Its batteries fire on enemies that come close.

hunt.d: Their flagship is running and jumps out at the end of round 6. Destroy it before then.

intercept.d: Enemy transports are crossing to the far side (red hexes). Destroy them before they get through.

break.d: Get ships off the far edge: a ship that ends its move on a green hex jumps clear. Their fleet blocks the way ahead and more close in from behind.

hold.d: Have a ship next to the relay, with no enemy there, at the start of 3 rounds.

flagship.d: Destroy their flagship and the rest of their fleet scatters.

hegemony.d: Ships within 3 hexes of their command ship gain aim and damage against targets another synced ship fired on this round. They can also back away for 1 movement instead of 2. Lose the command ship and sync is gone for the battle.

ithar.d: Shields refill at the start of a turn if the ship was not struck since its last turn. If struck, it gets only normal shield regen. Ships can slip away after firing, but cannot Brace.

chorus.d: Living ships regrow hull each round, and ship kills let the killer and nearby allies regrow more. Their own hulls have no shields.

deathless.d: An eligible fallen ship reassembles next round with 35% hull, but never the flagship. Fold drives pass through ships, rocks and wrecks at no extra cost. Eclipse hulls have no shields.

corsair.d: Boarding crews have extra strength, and rocket pods fire salvos that point defense can thin. Hullbreakers cannot field lance weapons.

voidsworn.d: Side guns hit harder after moving at least 2 hexes, and Brace covers one adjacent ally facing the same way. Carrier base prices have a 10% premium before rounding.

cut.w: cut in two by a lance

tidal.w: torn apart by the Hollow Sun

vex.d: Every ship fires a free volley at the best target its guns can reach, right now.

malek.d: Torpedoes reload at once and every ship deals +30% damage this round.

ashgrove.d: Every launch ship sends out an extra wing if there is room, then all squadrons strike again with +50% damage this round.

thale.d: All shields refill and your ships take 40% less hull damage this round.

tables.CMD_HOLD: Once per battle. Each round you hold it, it gets stronger (full power from round 3), and losing a ship charges it a level at once. Hold too long and the fight may be over.

aelith:cap:0.d: Your first wing strike each battle cannot miss and bypasses shields.

aelith:cap:1.d: The extra wing strike repeats at the start of the following round with the same damage bonus, if the wing still flies.

vaelen:cap:0.d: The concentrated target loses 10% armor for the rest of the battle (down to 0%).

vaelen:cap:1.d: The +15% damage mark applies to all your weapons against that target, not only lances.

thorne:cap:0.d: Triggers a second time on the first enemy shot of round 3.

thorne:cap:1.d: During the scatter round, the false images also draw away the first enemy torpedo volley.

mirelle:cap:0.d: The accuracy loss lasts for every shot that enemy fires this round, not only its next shot.

mirelle:cap:1.d: At round end while warded, leftover temporary hull also adds equal overshield (up to +25% max shields).

vex:cap:0.d: The enemy named on the roll cannot Brace this round.

vex:cap:1.d: A second kill from that extra shot grants one final follow-up shot (once per ship).

malek:cap:0.d: The second torpedo hits at full damage whenever it strikes a rear arc.

malek:cap:1.d: If the named prey survives, its damage mark carries into the next round at half strength.

ashgrove:cap:0.d: Wing fires spread to one adjacent hull section on the struck target.

ashgrove:cap:1.d: The escort wall intercepts two torpedoes per covered ship this round, not one.

thale:cap:0.d: Iron wall holds for a third round at half damage reduction.

thale:cap:1.d: Ships under the wall may also turn once for free each activation.

kassar:cap:0.d: One other synced ship also projects the sync net at normal radius.

kassar:cap:1.d: The named target also loses 15% armor for the rest of the round (down to 0%).

vorn:cap:0.d: The carried strike damage bonus lasts two rounds instead of one.

vorn:cap:1.d: The second shot deals full damage whenever it hits the same target as the first.

reyes:cap:0.d: The filed enemy's point defense is shut down for the rest of this round.

reyes:cap:1.d: Each patrol wing may trigger twice per round (once per enemy move).

maren:cap:0.d: Half of the extra hull damage reduction holds through the round after the wall ends.

maren:cap:1.d: Overshield from the line does not decay at round start while the flagship lives.

grax:cap:0.d: Rams during the carried burn round deal +25% damage.

grax:cap:1.d: Each boarding action the flagship lands repairs 10% of its hull.

sable:cap:0.d: That carried first rear-arc shot is always a critical hit.

sable:cap:1.d: Ships that make the 2-hex move also turn free toward the nearest foe and gain +10 aim this round.

mott:cap:0.d: Wings from the second launch strike at +15% damage.

mott:cap:1.d: Old Mott's private wing survives the first hit that would destroy it.

vesh:cap:0.d: Every restored section gains +20% armor for the rest of the battle.

vesh:cap:1.d: Nothing Stays Broken triggers twice per battle across your fleet.

matriarch:cap:0.d: The chosen enemy cannot spend movement or ram on its next turn.

matriarch:cap:1.d: Each extra swarm may chain its kill strike twice instead of once.

razormaw:cap:0.d: The +25% damage bonus covers every shot those ships fire next round.

razormaw:cap:1.d: Ships ending that move adjacent to the named prey deal +15% damage to it this round.

mending:cap:0.d: The end-of-round regrowth heals at full Command strength.

mending:cap:1.d: Any ship with a restored section regrows 2% max hull each round (once per ship).

voice:cap:0.d: The follow-up acid burst deals full damage to targets below half hull.

voice:cap:1.d: The chosen ship's acid hits also strip 10% armor for the battle (down to 0%).

nekhet:cap:0.d: The chosen ship also gains +10 evasion next round (within the 45 cap).

nekhet:cap:1.d: The repaired ship also resets its ability cooldown and takes 25% less hull damage until next round.

sekhmar:cap:0.d: Noon volley echoes a third round at quarter damage.

sekhmar:cap:1.d: The half-damage copy strikes the two enemies with the least hull, not one.

anuket:cap:0.d: Ships covered by the carried bonus also gain +10% critical chance.

anuket:cap:1.d: Ships that made the 2-hex move cannot be targeted past range 3 until they fire or the round ends.

khepra:cap:0.d: Half the hull damage blocked by the 25% cap returns as repair at next round start.

khepra:cap:1.d: Repaired ships keep the wall's hull damage reduction for two rounds after it ends.
